summary.text: Thurman Bill Bartie is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Randy Weber in Texas's 14th District. A lifelong Port Arthur resident, he has worked as a funeral director, teacher and pastor, was elected Justice of the Peace for Precinct 8 in Jefferson County in 1994, and served two terms as Mayor of Port Arthur. His campaign website lists economic opportunity, education, infrastructure and healthcare among his priorities.

paragraphs.text: Bartie is a lifelong resident of Port Arthur, Texas, and graduated from Lincoln High School.
He studied political science at Prairie View A&M University and earned a bachelor's degree from Lamar University.
He studied mortuary science at the Commonwealth College of Mortuary Science and became a licensed funeral director and embalmer.
He earned a master's degree in ministry from Tennessee Temple University Baptist Seminary.
His career experience includes working as a funeral director and embalmer at Hannah Funeral Home, as a teacher at Memorial High School, and as a pastor.
In 1994 he was elected the first African American Justice of the Peace for Precinct 8 in Jefferson County.
In 2019 he was elected Mayor of Port Arthur, defeating incumbent Derrick Freeman in a runoff, and served two terms.
In the 2026 Democratic primary he advanced to a runoff and defeated Richard Davis on May 26, 2026, with 51.0% of the vote.
